brand.vision: To create emotionally intelligent, climate-responsive and fully integrated homes for conscious families, NRIs and business leaders, bringing architecture, interiors, landscape, lighting, materials, craftsmanship and thoughtfully curated furniture together as one complete design experience.

before_you_begin.title: A Gentle Reminder Before You Begin
before_you_begin.subtitle: Building a home is one of life’s most significant decisions—the culmination of years of hard work, savings, dreams and emotion. Every member of your family carries their own hopes, routines, needs and quiet preferences. A truly meaningful home should thoughtfully hold space for all of them.

thoughts.title: You Matter in This Too
thoughts.content: While thinking about everyone else’s comfort, do not forget your own. Your peace of mind, daily rhythms and quiet vision of what 'home' should feel like matter just as much as anyone else’s.

thoughts.title: Tell Us How You Want to Feel
thoughts.content: As you describe your spaces, think beyond function, furniture and dimensions. Tell us how you want to feel the moment you walk in—calm, connected, protected, energised, inspired, welcomed or at peace. A feeling is as real a design requirement as a measurement.

thoughts.title: Speak Honestly About How You Live
thoughts.content: There are no right or wrong answers here. Tell us about your family’s real routines, habits, celebrations, work patterns, storage needs and everyday frustrations—not an idealised version of your lifestyle, but the life you genuinely live.

thoughts.title: Let Your Heart Choose, Not the Trend
thoughts.content: Trends fade, but the way a space makes you feel can stay with you for a lifetime. Choose what genuinely feels like you—not simply what appears fashionable, impressive or familiar from someone else’s home.

thoughts.title: Hold On to What Your Family Truly Wants
thoughts.content: Along the way, relatives and friends may offer plenty of well-meaning advice. Listen with respect, but remember that they will not live in this home or move through its spaces every day. The final decisions should primarily reflect the people who will actually live, grow, rest and gather here.

technical_glossary.natural_light: A design that brings sufficient daylight into the home through well-positioned windows, skylights, courtyards, and open spaces. Good natural light improves mood, supports a healthy sleep–wake cycle, reduces eye strain, and makes everyday activities more comfortable while reducing dependence on artificial lighting.
technical_glossary.skylight: A glazed opening provided in the roof or ceiling to bring daylight into the central areas of the home where regular windows may not reach. When properly positioned and shaded, it can make interior spaces feel brighter, more open, and welcoming without causing excessive heat.
technical_glossary.natural_ventilation: A design that allows fresh air to move naturally through the home using properly placed windows, ventilators, courtyards, and open passages. Continuous airflow helps remove indoor heat, odours, excess moisture, carbon dioxide, and pollutants, supporting better breathing, concentration, sleep quality, and overall comfort.
technical_glossary.cross_ventilation: A method of placing openings on opposite or adjacent sides of a room so that fresh air enters through one opening and warm or stale air exits through another. This continuous air movement helps keep the room cooler, fresher, and more comfortable naturally.
technical_glossary.passive_cooling: A climate-responsive design approach that reduces indoor heat through proper building orientation, shaded openings, deep roof overhangs, suitable materials, greenery, and natural airflow. It keeps the home naturally cooler, improves daily comfort, reduces excessive dependence on air-conditioning, lowers energy consumption, and creates a healthier living environment.
technical_glossary.cavity_wall: A wall constructed with an air gap between two layers. This gap acts as a thermal barrier, slowing the transfer of outdoor heat into the interior and helping rooms remain cooler. Proper waterproofing and moisture detailing are essential, especially in Kerala’s hot and humid climate.
technical_glossary.louvers_sunshades: Horizontal or vertical shading elements placed outside windows to block harsh direct sunlight while still allowing fresh air and soft, diffused daylight to enter. They reduce heat gain, improve indoor comfort, protect windows from rain, and reduce the need for air-conditioning.
technical_glossary.zoning: Dividing the house into three types of areas — private zones (bedrooms), social zones (living, dining), and service zones (kitchen, utility) — so each area functions without disturbing the others.
technical_glossary.mep: Mechanical, Electrical and Plumbing — the complete engineering design of your electrical wiring, water supply, drainage, and any HVAC (air conditioning) systems.
technical_glossary.layered_lighting: A design approach using four complementary layers — ambient (general room light), task (focused light for reading, cooking, work), accent (highlighting art, niches, textures) and decorative (statement fixtures) — combined so each space feels balanced, functional and visually rich rather than flatly lit by a single source.
technical_glossary.home_automation: The use of connected systems — lighting, climate, curtains, security and audio — controlled centrally through an app, touch panel or voice assistant, either as a fully integrated whole-home system or selectively for specific functions.
technical_glossary.tensile_structure: A shading canopy made of stretched PVC or PTFE fabric supported by cables and columns — lightweight, modern-looking, and drains rainwater easily.
